description: Parties acting on data-center and energy projects, the register's starting watch list. Each action cites its source; projects and claims are recorded with claims-project-record and claims-claim-record as they are read from dockets.

parties.action: Tribal Council unanimously enacted a moratorium on data-center development within tribal lands and territories, after a start-up company asked the Nation for a non-disclosure agreement.

Tribal Council passed a resolution opposing "the irresponsible development of hyperscale data centers" and a moratorium on its nearly one-million-acre reservation, which shares a 108-mile border with the Colorado River.

Principal Chief Chuck Hoskin Jr. issued Executive Order 2026-02-CTH establishing a task force to evaluate the economic and environmental effects of data centers within the Cherokee Nation Reservation.

context.finding: Data-center developers are courting Native nations as a lighter regulatory path than municipalities tightening their codes.

Data Center Watch's first-quarter 2026 report puts blocked or delayed projects at about $130 billion in one quarter; Gallup (2026-05-13) finds 71% of Americans oppose a local AI data center; STL Partners prices a month of delay at a typical 60 MW site at $14.2 million.

Across 33 captured or contested projects, the capturing moves cluster in county rezoning and annexation votes and in review-adequacy lawsuits, while developers' messaging spends itself on decorative claims (jobs, economic impact).
